Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Fix GitHub issue #244 in Moneo: generate a feature map of pages, widgets, chat tools and commands. The owner chose this design:
- `npm run feature-map` generates `FEATURES.md` from the registries that already exist: App Router routes, chat tool registrations (lib/ai), voice tools, home widgets, the command palette, workflows and cron routes, and undo paths where represented. Don't hand-maintain a second catalogue.
- Regeneration is deterministic: sorted, with no timestamps.
- CI fails when `FEATURES.md` is stale. Add the check to the existing `checks` job, or as a script run by `npm run lint` or `npm test`. The failure message says to run `npm run feature-map`.
- Keep the map compact: per feature, its entry points (page, chat tool, voice, widget, palette, background job) and the main code paths.
- Never include private data, env values or credentials.
- The verify-ui and state-chart skills can refer to it. Add one line to AGENTS.md "Hit every surface" pointing to FEATURES.md, plus a rules-table row for the staleness check.
- Don't write tests that grep implementation text. The generator reads registries as data.

## Rules
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly. Read `gh issue view 244`.
- Branch `t3/issue-244-feature-map` from current `origin/main`. Commit each step, ending each message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Don't end your turn while a command is still running.** Wait for it in the same turn.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start yourself in this session, verified by PID.**
- Run one `npm ci` at a time. If it stalls, retry once with `--prefer-offline`.
- Shared test backend: never run `npm run qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`, and never touch the owner's backend.
- **Run `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` yourself and quote their last lines in your final reply.** Also run `npm test` and `npm run build`.
- Push and open a PR to `main` (`Closes #244`), ending the body with:
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  Never merge.
- Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

**Priority:** P2 (incremental follow-up).

## Problem and current evidence

The Hit every surface checklist relies on an agent remembering related entry points. The audit proposed a feature map to provide shared vocabulary and discover disconnected surfaces.

## Scope

Use existing route/tool/widget/palette registries as inputs. Generate a compact map of user features, entry points and relevant code, including voice, artifacts, background work and undo where represented. Prefer structured existing registrations over a second hand-maintained catalogue. Check registry/map consistency without tests that grep implementation text.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New registered surfaces appear automatically or produce a clear consistency failure.
- [ ] The map helps an agent locate UI, chat, voice and reverse paths for a feature.
- [ ] No private data or runtime credentials are included.
- [ ] A documented command regenerates the map deterministically.
- [ ] verify-ui and state-chart workflows can reference the map without growing AGENTS.md with feature-specific instructions.

## Verification and constraints

Reproduce the current behaviour before changing it. Run the smallest relevant check during implementation, then npm test, npm run lint and npm run typecheck; add a build for app/config changes and real QA browser verification for changed user flows. Use only disposable moneo-qa services, synthetic records and mocked paid integrations. Verify source installation and desktop compatibility. Preserve financial history, corrections and undo. Do not add prose or comments in place of a deterministic boundary.

## Delivery

This issue records follow-up work; it does not claim the change is implemented. Recheck current main and #224 before starting, since the audit counts may have changed. Keep the PR focused and link its checks and relevant evidence here.

>
